info.title: TelltaleDNS API
info.description: Read and control a TelltaleDNS resolver. JSON is camelCase; field names carry units (`totalMs`, `ttlSeconds`). Errors are RFC 9457 problem+json with a stable `code` and a `hint`. Time parameters take RFC 3339 or a relative offset (`-24h`). Collections page with `cursor`/`limit`. Analytics calls take `scope` (`cluster` or `node:local`; both mean this node until clustering is available).

post.description:
Username and password, plus `totp` (or `recoveryCode`) when two-factor sign-in is on:
without it the answer is 401 `totp_required`. Sets an `HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict` session
cookie and returns the CSRF token to send as `X-CSRF-Token` on changes. Repeated failures
lock the username and the address out for a while (429).
Ends this session and clears the cookie. With a token or Basic, does nothing but succeed.

get.description:
The signed-in user: role (capped by a token's scope), two-factor state, unused recovery
codes, and how this request authenticated.

post.description: Needs the current password. Ends every other session of this user.

Only while no user exists. `setupToken` is printed in the server log at startup and saved
in `<data_dir>/setup-token`. Signs the new admin in (sets the session cookie).

get.description:
Whether first-run setup is needed, and who the request is signed in as (if anyone),
with the session's CSRF token. Public; the UI calls it on load.

post.description: Needs the current password. Removes the TOTP secret and the unused recovery codes.

Confirms a current code from the app enrolled with POST /auth/totp/setup, turns
enforcement on, and returns ten single-use recovery codes (shown only now).

Returns a new TOTP secret (base32 and an `otpauth://` URL for a QR code). Nothing is
enforced until POST /auth/totp/enable confirms a code from the app.

get.summary: Configured clients (devices) and how they're recognized.
get.description:
Each device's name, the IPs, CIDRs, MACs, or client IDs that identify it, and its groups in
priority order (the first group's settings apply). Unknown devices use the `default` group.

Why `name` is or isn't blocked for a client: how the client is identified, its groups,
every matching rule in every list (with the list line), which rule decides, and where the
query would be forwarded. Example: `GET /api/v1/explain?name=ads.example.com&client=192.168.1.20`.

parameters.name: mac
parameters.description: The client's MAC address (default: from the neighbor table).

get.summary: Client groups, their lists, block mode, and pause state.
get.description:
Groups decide which lists apply to a device and how blocked queries are answered. `lists`
null means every enabled list; `pausedUntilUnixSeconds` is set while blocking is paused.

get.summary: Filter lists and their download state.
get.description:
Every configured list with its kind (block/allow), source, download state (`ok`, `failed`,
`pending`) and last error, size, and how many names it contributes to the active snapshot.

Newest first. Filters combine with AND: name (substring by default; `match=exact|suffix|
glob|regex`), client, status, query type, response code, upstream, minimum latency, and
time range. Pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` for older rows. Example:
`GET /api/v1/queries?name=doubleclick&status=blocked&from=-1h&limit=50`.

parameters.name: minLatencyMs
parameters.description: Only queries that took at least this long.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start: RFC 3339 or relative (`-1h`). Default: no limit.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Continue after a previous page (`nextCursor` from it).

get.description:
By answer path and transport, query type, upstream server, or the upstream stage, for the
current or previous hour, in milliseconds (HDR histograms, 2 significant digits).

Queries, blocked (count and percent), cache hits, forwarded, NXDOMAIN and SERVFAIL counts
from the minute series (the last 48 hours), plus this hour's active clients and latency
percentiles by answer path. Example: `GET /api/v1/stats/summary?from=-24h`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start: RFC 3339 or relative (`-24h`). Default: 24 hours ago (at most 48 hours back).

get.description:
Buckets by status, query type, and response code, plus upstream exchanges. `step=second`
covers the last 15 minutes, `step=minute` the last 48 hours. Example:
`GET /api/v1/stats/timeseries?from=-1h&step=minute`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description:
Start: RFC 3339 or relative (`-1h`). Default: 1 hour ago (minute steps) or 5 minutes
ago (second steps).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End: RFC 3339 or relative. Default: now.

get.summary: Top domains, blocked domains, NXDOMAIN names, or clients.
get.description:
Ranked by a Space-Saving sketch per hour: `count` is an upper bound and `errorBound` how
far it may be over. Example: `GET /api/v1/stats/top?kind=blocked&limit=10`. With
`kind=domains&client=192.168.1.20`, one client's top domains (recently active clients only).

parameters.name: client
parameters.description: Only this client's domains (an IP address; `kind=domains` only).

get.description:
Version, role, uptime, listeners, whether the query log is on, and the active filter
snapshot. Cheap; suitable for health dashboards.
Name, scope, expiry, and last use. The secrets themselves are never shown again.

post.description:
For scripts, dashboards, and agents: send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. `scope`
`read` acts as viewer, `write` as operator, `admin` as admin, never above the owner's role.
The token is shown only in this response.

delete.summary: Revoke one of my API tokens.
delete.description: By the `id` from GET /tokens. Takes effect immediately; other tokens are unaffected.

get.summary: Upstream servers with health and latency.
get.description:
Every upstream with its stable ID, endpoint, groups, circuit-breaker state (`closed` means
healthy), request and failure counts, and smoothed answer time in milliseconds.
Every user with role, status, and two-factor state.

post.description: `role` is `viewer`, `operator`, or `admin`. The password needs at least 10 characters.

delete.description: Also deletes their sessions and tokens. The last enabled admin can't be deleted.

patch.description:
Role, disabled, HTTP Basic opt-in, a new password (ends their sessions), or a TOTP reset.
The last enabled admin can't be demoted or disabled.

AuthStatus.description: Whether setup is needed and who is signed in (public).

csrfToken.description: For session sign-ins: send as `X-CSRF-Token` on changes.

setupRequired.description: No user exists yet: create the first admin with the setup token.

match.description: IPs, CIDRs, MACs, or `id:<client-id>` this device is recognized by.

allowBasicApi.description: Allow HTTP Basic on the API for scripts and scrapers (default false).

device.description: The configured device it was recognized as.

routed.description: An explicit route matched (not just the default group).

enabled.description: The client's groups use this list.

lines.description: Where the rule is in the list.

Explanation.description: Why a name is or isn't blocked for a client, and where it would go (FLT-013).

oneOf.description: Every matching rule in precedence order; absent until a filter is loaded.

pausedUntilUnixSeconds.description: Blocking is paused for this client until then (Unix seconds).

lists.description: Lists this group uses; null means every enabled list.

pausedUntilUnixSeconds.description: Blocking is paused for this group until then (Unix seconds).

Hour.description: Which hour a top-K or latency call reads.

Items_ClientInfo.description: A list wrapper used by every collection endpoint.

match.description: IPs, CIDRs, MACs, or `id:<client-id>` this device is recognized by.

Items_GroupInfo.description: A list wrapper used by every collection endpoint.

lists.description: Lists this group uses; null means every enabled list.

pausedUntilUnixSeconds.description: Blocking is paused for this group until then (Unix seconds).

Items_LatencyRow.description: A list wrapper used by every collection endpoint.

items.description: Latency percentiles for one key (HDR histogram, 2 significant digits).

Items_ListInfo.description: A list wrapper used by every collection endpoint.

items.description: A filter list and its download state.

entries.description: Names this list contributes to the active snapshot.

Items_TimeBucket.description: A list wrapper used by every collection endpoint.

upstreamQueries.description: Upstream exchanges, and how many failed.

Items_TopItem.description: A list wrapper used by every collection endpoint.

items.description:
One ranked item. Counts come from a Space-Saving sketch: the true count lies in
`[count - errorBound, count]`.

name.description: The configured device name, for clients that have one.

Items_UpstreamInfo.description: A list wrapper used by every collection endpoint.

items.description: An upstream server and its health.

id.description: Stable ID (config order, from 1); query rows and latency rows refer to it.

LatencyRow.description: Latency percentiles for one key (HDR histogram, 2 significant digits).

ListInfo.description: A filter list and its download state.

entries.description: Names this list contributes to the active snapshot.

totp.description: 6-digit code from the authenticator app, when TOTP is on.

csrfToken.description: Send as `X-CSRF-Token` on every change made with this session.

recoveryCodesLeft.description: Unused recovery codes (when TOTP is on).

role.description: Effective role (a token's scope caps its owner's role).

token.description: The token, shown only now: send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

detail.description: What went wrong in this request.

title.description: Short, human-readable summary of the problem type.

example.detail: `from`: `yesterday`: expected RFC 3339 time (2026-10-03T12:00:00Z) or a relative offset (-24h)
example.hint: Use a relative offset such as -24h, or RFC 3339 such as 2026-10-03T00:00:00Z.
example.title: Invalid parameter

QueryPage.description: A page of query-log rows, newest first.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to get older rows; absent when there are none.

scanned.description: How much of the log this page looked at.

clientName.description: The configured device name, when known.

list.description: The list whose rule blocked or allowed the query.

rcode.description: Response code, or null when nothing was sent.

Scope.description: An API token's scope; a token never exceeds its owner's role.

cacheHitPercent.description: Cache share of answered queries that weren't blocked or local, 0–100.

latency.description: Latency percentiles this hour, by answer path (`cache`, `upstream`, ...).

filterNames.description: Blocked names in the active snapshot.

filterSnapshot.description: Version of the active filter snapshot, if one is loaded.

queryLog.description: Whether the per-query log is being written.

upstreamQueries.description: Upstream exchanges, and how many failed.

TopItem.description:
One ranked item. Counts come from a Space-Saving sketch: the true count lies in
`[count - errorBound, count]`.

name.description: The configured device name, for clients that have one.

secretBase32.description: For manual entry in an authenticator app.

password.description: Set a new password (ends the user's sessions).

resetTotp.description: Turn off the user's TOTP (if they lost their device).

UpstreamInfo.description: An upstream server and its health.

id.description: Stable ID (config order, from 1); query rows and latency rows refer to it.

tags.name: stats
tags.description: Live counters, top lists, and latency percentiles from memory (the last 48 hours at minute resolution, 15 minutes at second resolution).

tags.name: queries
tags.description: The query log and explanations of decisions.

tags.name: config
tags.description: Lists, groups, clients, and upstreams as running.

tags.name: auth
tags.description: Sign-in, two-factor, API tokens, and users. Everything else needs one of: the session cookie from POST /auth/login (plus X-CSRF-Token on changes), Authorization: Bearer <token>, or HTTP Basic for users who allow it.
